inspection_outcome: Verified GCD feasible-set/attainment failure and repairable display errors
summary: The fixed-grade singular matrix model permits common roots at infinity; the ordinary GCD problem stated in Section7 does not. A unique relaxed optimum can be inadmissible and the original infimum unattained.
limitations: No published numerical benchmark error established.
No global replacement GCD algorithm or attainment theorem supplied.

problems.title: Degree-drop boundary invalidates approximate GCD equivalence

source_claim.locator: Section7 PDF pp.25-26, equation(16) and S_d reduction
source_claim.text: Ordinary GCD degree at least d is equivalent to fixed-grade S_d singularity, so the minimization can be recast as structured matrix nearness.

assumptions: p=tx+1,q=tx-1,0<t<1,m=n=d=1, over real subset of complex field
Both original leading coefficients nonzero; all exhibited perturbations have exact degree1 as stated

check.type: Exact analytic finite-dimensional counterexample and infimum calculation
steps: S1=[[1,-1],[t,t]] has orthogonal rows and singular values sqrt2,sqrt2*t.
Unique nearest rank<=1 matrix S0=[[1,-1],[0,0]] at distance sqrt2*t, verified by null-vector norm lower bound and equality conditions.
S0 corresponds to constants1,-1, whose ordinary GCD has degree0.
Feasible pairs (1+hx,-1-hx) for0<|h|<t have distance sqrt(2t²+2h²), so original infimum sqrt2*t is approached.
Any attaining feasible pair must equal unique S0, impossible; original min not attained.
check.result: Claimed feasible-set and minimum/argmin equivalence false at permitted degree-drop boundary.

counterevidence: Homogeneous fixed-grade GCD would count the common infinite root, but changes the stated ordinary GCD problem.
The paper p38 and code example_zeng2.m reconstruct factors and compute residuals; no historical benchmark falsified.

impact.dependency: Section7 ordinary-GCD definition -> fixed-size S_d singularity -> application of central oracle framework and nearest_gcd.m.
impact.scope: Material application equivalence and attainment claim; not failure of entire Riemann-Oracle.

correction.statement: Specify homogeneous closure versus ordinary affine GCD, and analyze boundary/attainment or add appropriate closed coefficient constraints.
correction.verification: Boundary failure and nonattainment proven; merely nonzero perturbed leading coefficients insufficient.
correction.limits: No complete corrected general algorithm or theorem established.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed for actual ordinary C[x] GCD and allowable perturbations of the input degrees. For p=tx+1,q=tx-1,0<t<1, the unique nearest singular fixed-size matrix removes the degree-one row and gives constants 1,-1, whose GCD degree is zero. Feasible pairs 1+hx,-1-hx approach its distance sqrt(2)t but do not attain it. A nonvanishing-leading-coefficient restriction would be open and would not restore attainment; homogeneous fixed-grade closure changes the problem. Source p.38 and example_zeng2 explicitly reconstruct factors and residuals, limiting the numerical allegation.

problems.title: Sparse objective and gradient weight errors

source_claim.text: With d_i=sum_J |v_j|², uses h_i=(d_i²+epsilon)^(-1/2) in norm objective and h in first gradient term.

counterevidence: Pinned nearest_singular_sparse.m uses D=1/(d+epsilon), correct cost/gradient/Hessian; no executed experimental discrepancy established.

impact.dependency: Sparse specialization of valid general oracle
impact.scope: Display errors directly repairable; current experiment route uses correct formula

correction.statement: Set h_i=(d_i+epsilon)^(-1/2), use h_i² in first gradient term.
correction.verification: Algebraically verified; statically matches pinned code.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed analytically. With diagonal sparsity, A=diag(1,2), v=(1,1)/sqrt(2), epsilon=1 and y=0, the correct objective is 5/3, whereas the printed h gives 2. The correct gradient is (8/9)(1,4)/sqrt(2); the printed expression gives (4/sqrt(5)-4/9)(1,4)/sqrt(2), with nonzero tangential discrepancy. The retained sparse code uses 1/(d+epsilon) and the correct z expression.

problems.title: Squared-objective bound missing a square

source_claim.text: Bound for squared f ends with ||alpha||.

steps: Orthogonal projection gives f(v)=||M^dagger M alpha||²<=||alpha||².
check.result: Printed bound false, squared corrected bound valid.

counterevidence: Boundedness argument is retained with corrected exponent.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed directly for the squared objective: scalar structured A=2 has minimum 4, exceeding the printed norm(alpha)=2. Squaring the coefficient norm repairs the bound.

positive_checks.evidence: Complete-square/SVD/directional calculations in report section2; code correspondence checked statically.
Completed square and rank-at-most condition checked with stated uniqueness/real-coefficient restrictions.

focused_acceptance_summary.scope: Focused acceptance of the three reported Problems only: the ordinary-polynomial GCD formulation at degree loss, the sparse objective/gradient displays, and the missing square in the bound. Exact counterexamples and code/text counterevidence were independently checked. The retained author repository was statically read, not executed, and its later commit is not treated as the historical experiment revision.
focused_acceptance_summary.assessment_review: Retain Major for the false equivalence and attained-minimum claim in the approximate-GCD application. Retain Minor for the displayed sparse formulas and missing square. Explicit factor reconstruction is preserved as counterevidence to allegations about the published benchmark distances; the general Riemannian method is not refuted.
